summary: Fresh source review found no concrete blocking defect in this bounded two-condition gradient diagnostic. The manual full and RGB-only partial loss/backward matches the demo_shared path of run_shared_identity_experiment.step before its unscale/optimizer actions. Both conditions reuse one warm model and one augmented B64/P8/K8 batch, reload its complete registered initial state and reset seed42. Only the process-local available_base_fusion binding is changed; no optimizer, weight save, evaluation, training acceptance waiver or formal training launch is implemented. This review did not execute the diagnostic.

evidence: run_rgbnt201_original_anchor.py:19 delegates to run_shared_identity_experiment.step; shared_identity_axis.py supplies the model and partial_gallery_triplet, not the step itself.
SharedIdentityDeMo with RGBNT201 DIRECT=1 returns four score/feature pairs and loss_weights [1, 1, 0.25, 1]: fused, MoE, common shared head, and concatenated original globals.

diagnose_rgbnt201_fusion_precision.py:66-74 reproduces the weighted full loss and detached output[1] reference used by run_shared_identity_experiment.py:40-52. The demo_shared model returns no odd trailing contribution loss.
The reused make_loss uses RGBNT201 ID_LOSS_WEIGHT=0.25, TRIPLET_LOSS_WEIGHT=1, label smoothing on and the configured soft triplet.
Probe lines75-82 retain RGB and zero NI/TI, reproducing retained=(0,) in the native verifier. They reuse the same label-smoothed CE and partial_gallery_triplet with weights 0.25 and 0.5.
partial_gallery_triplet detaches the full reference, excludes each query itself from positives, uses GT labels and retains the existing positive/negative mining and FP32 distance computation.

original_identity_anchor.build loads original RGBNT201 demo best.pth and checks the completed50 result, native exit, 2647 optimizer steps, zero skipped steps, no heldout identities, classes/cameras and official manifest.
The archived original result independently records selected epoch28, 171 training identities, four camera embeddings, and completed50.
Probe lines43-49 create one adaptive model, clone state_dict tensors to CPU, and load one augmented batch once. Both conditions reuse these exact tensors.
Probe lines62-65 strictly reload parameters and registered buffers, select train mode, clear gradients and reset all existing Python/NumPy/Torch/CUDA seed sources to42 before each full forward.
configuration plus RGBNT201 YAML sets B64/K8; the unchanged RandomIdentitySampler constructs eight groups of eight identities/instances. The probe asserts B64 and eight unique identities.
full_records uses all3951 official training records and all836 query/836 gallery metadata with zero artificial holdout. Only a single training batch undergoes neural computation in this diagnostic.
Probe lines52-61 capture the actual shared module function then bind either that original or an autocast-disabled wrapper calling the same function with FP32 patch/global inputs.
SharedIdentityDeMo.forward reaches encode_available, whose module-global available_base_fusion lookup observes this binding for both full and partial calls.

No parameter dtype or requires_grad flag is changed by the wrapper. Input float casts preserve autograd connectivity. build returns FP32 parameters, so the disabled region supports FP32 fusion operations.

CLIP, reductions, shared projection, heads and losses retain their original outer autocast contexts and existing explicit FP32 subregions. The fusion result can propagate normal dtype promotion; this is a local precision intervention, not a claim that every downstream operation is FP16.
The original function binding is restored on normal completion. Only this isolated process is affected; runtime source files are not edited.
Both backward calls multiply loss by exactly512, matching the fixed initial GradScaler512 pre-unscale gradient calculation in the failed native attempt. No optimizer is created or called.
gradient_state enumerates every requires_grad named parameter, distinguishes None, nonfinite and finite-zero gradients, records parameter/gradient dtype and all nonzero counts.

Stored gradient tensors are still scaled512. max_abs is divided by512 in the report; finite/nonzero counts are observations on the scaled tensors. This is not an executed GradScaler.unscale_/step or a replacement native acceptance check.

Probe lines84-86 compare every named parameter with its saved initial CPU tensor after each condition. BN buffers are expected to change within a train-mode condition and are restored before the next condition.
No torch.save, optimizer update or checkpoint overwrite occurs. Each condition has its own JSON and the terminal result has diagnostic COMPLETE status, not a native/smoke PASS.
Only one live model and a CPU state snapshot are held; no Adam states, second model, replay model or saved weight binary is created.

The full backward runs before the RGB partial forward and output is deleted, preserving the existing B64 activation-release design. Per-condition graph values are deleted before the next iteration; retained measurements are plain scalar dictionaries.
FP32 fusion uses more temporary memory than AMP fusion; source review does not establish its actual peak or completion. Native execution remains required to observe this.
The fresh output directory uses exist_ok=False, preserving earlier failure outputs. Per-condition reports persist independently, and result.json is written only after both conditions finish.
The terminal limits explicitly deny completed50/all49, validation score, method-gain and acceptance-gate claims and acknowledge stochastic kernels can differ across dtypes.

The supplied initial command omitted training/ in the anchor path. Existing rgbnt201_original_anchor_deploy_20261005.py ANCHOR and archived baseline layout establish the corrected path below; the probe itself accepts and uses --anchor-run-dir correctly.

original_identity_anchor.build checks CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES through the existing GPU2/3 memory-only check. The proposed bounded execution uses gpu_thermal_execute.execute(..., gpu=2), which exports physical2 as visible CUDA and records launch/exit.
gpu_thermal_execute retains 240-second memory-availability waits and contains no temperature/power queries or conditions. This review did not invoke it or independently query remote hardware.

preserved_prior_failure.acceptance_gate: Unchanged: every active parameter must have a finite nonzero native gradient; the prior adaptive failure is not waived.

validation.review_execution: Read-only source/artifact inspection plus stdlib AST, JSON and SHA256 operations; only this review JSON was written.
validation.local_parser: Existing uv-managed CPython3.12 executable; bare python alias was unusable (No pyvenv.cfg file) before any script execution. No environment installation or repair.

interpretation_limits: SOURCE_REVIEW_PASS authorizes no claim of runtime completion, corrected native preflight, successful optimization, formal50 or all49 results.

A difference on one warm-start training batch supports a precision-sensitivity diagnosis only. Attention/dropout kernels and their random-number consumption may differ despite equal seeds; the comparison cannot by itself prove a unique underflow mechanism or scientific improvement.
Any prospective training precision change still needs its own source review and the unchanged actual native/smoke gates before formal training.
